This Petition Coming On For Orders This
Day, B.M. Shyam Prasad J., Made The Following:
 Order

The complainant, who asserts that the land measuring 03 acres 38 guntas in Sy.No.237/2 of Saradagi village, Kalaburagi taluka and district is submerged with the construction of a barrage, has filed a representation for acquisition of land and payment of compensation.

Subsequently, the complainant has filed her writ petition in W.P.No.200843/2021 for directions to the respondents to consider the representation, and the writ Court, by its order dated 20.01.2022, has disposed of this writ petition directing the respondents therein to consider the complainant's representation within three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of the NC: 2023:KHC-K:1253-DB order.
The complainant alleges that there is deliberate disobedience of this order.

2. During the present proceedings, it was stated on behalf of the revenue authorities that the complainant, because she is unable to explain ownership to the subject property, would not be entitled for any consideration.

This Court has enabled the complainant to file a set of documents to establish her title to the subject land, and with the complainant filing a set of documents, the Deputy Commissioner, Kalaburagi - the first respondent, was called upon to verify the documents furnished, and to take appropriate decision and file compliance report or otherwise.

3. It is now stated in unison that the revenue authorities have completed the proceedings and it is ascertained that the complainant is indeed the owner of the subject land; that the Deputy Commissioner has conducted appropriate proceedings in the presence of all the concerned including the complainant and determined NC: 2023:KHC-K:1253-DB that the complainant would be entitled for compensation in a total sum of Rs.1,00,90,200/-.

It is further submitted in unison that pursuant to this decision in the proceedings, the Commissioner, City Municipal Corporation, Kalaburagi - the fifth respondent will have to initiate appropriate proceedings with the State Government to secure fund allocation and disburse the amount in accordance with law.

4. When queried, Sri Gourish S. Khashampur, the learned standing counsel for the fifth respondent,
submits that as only a sum about Rs.4 lakhs is deposited under the erstwhile Land Acquisition Act,
there will have to be necessary correspondence and every effort would be made to see to it that the amount as agreed in the proceedings is disbursed to the complainant.

These submissions are considered in the light of the proceedings dated 15.06.2023, which is one of the documents placed Pramilabai @ Parimalabai W/O ... vs Yashwanth Gurukar And Ors on 20 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52792849/
3 on record to report compliance.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:1253-DB 5.

The complainant, who has participated in the proceedings, has agreed to receive compensation in a total sum of Rs.1,00,90,200/- undertaking that she will not avail further remedy if the aforesaid sum is paid in terms of the decision in the meeting.

In the light of this undertaking and closure of controversy to the satisfaction of the concerned, there must be expedited measures to ensure that the complainant is paid the total sum of Rs.1,00,90,200/- in terms of the decision now taken, and six months, given the circumstances of the case, will not be very unreasonable.

Hence, the proceedings stand dropped reserving liberty to the complainant to work out her remedies in the event the sum of Rs.1,00,90,200/- is not within a period of 06 [six] months from today in terms of the decision taken in the meeting held on 15.06.2023.
